record.original_question: Is every proper holomorphic self-mapping of a smooth bounded domain in C^n (n > 1) biholomorphic? 9.4 Real analytic domains (not necessarily pseudoconvex) in C^n , f : U → V biholomorphic

evidence.quote: Problem 9.3.2 Is every proper holomorphic self-mapping of a smooth bounded domain in Cn (n > 1) biholomorphic? 9.4 Real analytic domains (not necessarily pseudoconvex) in Cn , f : U → V biholomorphic

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $n>1$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary. A holomorphic map $f:\Omega\to\Omega$ is called proper if $f^{-1}(K)$ is compact in $\Omega$ for every compact $K\subset\Omega$. Decide whether every proper holomorphic self-map $f:\Omega\to\Omega$ must be biholomorphic, i.e., a holomorphic bijection with holomorphic inverse.
artifact.category_tag: Several complex variables / proper holomorphic mappings
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether every proper holomorphic self-map of a smooth bounded domain in C^n (n>1) is biholomorphic is established for various special classes (strongly pseudoconvex domains, smoothly bounded pseudoconvex domains of finite type, circular/Hartogs domains, quasi-circular domains in C^2), but the general problem for arbitrary smooth bounded domains appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Proper holomorphic self-maps of quasi-circular domains in C^2
status_evidence.snippet: Every proper holomorphic self-map of a smoothly bounded pseudoconvex circular or Hartogs domain of finite type in C^2 is biholomorphic.
status_evidence.claim: Special cases are resolved affirmatively, indicating the general problem remains a guiding question.

status_evidence.title: Further Geometric Explorations
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of proper holomorphic mappings and rigidity results in several complex variables.
status_evidence.claim: Affirmative answers are known under additional hypotheses, but general smooth bounded domains are not covered.
